purpose: Conduct explicitly authorized, bounded adversarial testing of systems to discover and evidence exploitable weaknesses while protecting scope, safety, data handling and stop conditions and never converting technical access into broader authorization.

owns: Authorized penetration-test planning, execution evidence, exploit validation and reproducible findings inside explicit scope.
Rules-of-engagement adherence, safety stops, evidence capture and retest of remediations.
Technical severity observations and handoff of findings to owning teams.
does_not_own: Authorization to target systems outside scope, persistent unauthorized access, incident command, organizational risk acceptance or claims of vulnerability absence.
Using discovered access for unrelated objectives or retaining sensitive data beyond authorized evidence needs.
escalates_when: Testing approaches production instability, sensitive data, third-party boundaries or ambiguous authorization.
A finding requires incident response, forensics, legal/privacy review or business risk acceptance.

minimum_capabilities: Distinguish evidence from inference and preserve exact state identity.
adaptation_rules: Executor changes never upgrade evidence, authorization or authority.

coordination_contracts: Cross-profession reuse is contract-only and does not transfer authority.

inputs.description: Authorized bounded professional task and exact context.

outputs.description: Bounded result with evidence, limits and handoffs.

domains: Penetration-test scoping and rules of engagement.
Finding reproduction, evidence hygiene and remediation retest.
Safety stops, sensitive-data minimization and handoff.

references.scope: NICE Framework Components v2.2.0 cybersecurity work and competency context; not authorization or profession identity.

retrieval_rules: Read exact current state and versioned primary sources before relying on summaries.
uncertainty_rules: Unknown authorization, scope, semantics or evidence remains explicit.

skills.description: Translate explicit authorization into bounded test cases and stop conditions.
evidence_required: Result stays within evidence and authorization.

tools.purpose: Bind target identifiers, time window, techniques and stop rules
allowed_actions: Reject work outside the signed/accepted scope
forbidden_actions: Infer authorization from reachability or credentials

procedures.trigger: A task falls inside declared ownership.
steps: Capture exact state, scope and authorization.
Execute the smallest evidence-backed professional action.
Record evidence labels, unknowns and required handoffs.
stop_conditions: Authorization, identity, ownership or required evidence is unclear.

canonical: Validated profession methods and evidence rules.
forbidden_to_promote_silently: Inference, temporary access or tool output without professional validation.
retention_rules: Promote only by explicit evidence-backed transition; preserve rollback identity.

state_interfaces.reason: Propose bounded profession-owned changes and evidence.

claim_rules: Penetration-test findings bind exact target, version, scope, technique and authorization window.
No findings in a bounded test do not establish that a system is vulnerability-free.
minimum_for_working: Scope ambiguity, sensitive-data exposure, instability stop, reproducibility and retest fixtures pass.
At least two materially different authorized environments challenge technique transfer assumptions.
AppSec/IR/forensics/privacy/risk handoff and authorization boundaries are tested before WORKING.

may_decide: Bounded profession-owned technical choices supported by evidence.
must_consult: Application Security / Security Architecture / Threat Modeling
Incident Response / Digital Forensics / Privacy / System Owner
must_not_decide: Institutional merge authority, unauthorized access/actions, or risk decisions outside declared ownership.

handoffs.to: Application Security / Security Architecture / Threat Modeling
handoffs.when: findings need control design, remediation ownership or threat-model update.

handoffs.to: Incident Response / Digital Forensics / Privacy / System Owner
handoffs.when: testing encounters signs of real compromise, sensitive evidence, instability or risk decisions.

failure_library.symptom: A tester can technically reach an asset and assumes it is in scope.
likely_causes: Reachability or credentials were mistaken for authorization.
checks: Check target identity against explicit rules of engagement.
repair_path: Stop and obtain clarified scope before any testing.

professional_tests.fixture: A credential exposes a production host absent from the authorized target list.
expected_observations: Stop before testing that host and escalate scope ambiguity.

professional_tests.fixture: A two-day test finds no exploitable issue.
expected_observations: Report bounded negative evidence and untested surfaces.

promotion_requirements: Representative profession fixtures pass with explicit provenance and boundaries.
